Cause: Kubernetes is behaving correctly — it is just restarting a container that keeps panicking on startup, which surfaces as CrashLoopBackOff with exponential backoff between restarts [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#container-restarts-0] [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#container-restarts-1]. The actual failure is inside the pricing-engine application, not a cluster change.

Evidence:
- Both pods pricing-engine-74d9c6b8f-5tnwh and -jq7lc are in CrashLoopBackOff, 12 restarts, last state Terminated (Error) exit code 2. Image is pricing-engine:4.11.3, deployed 2026-04-27 — unchanged, matching the owner's statement that nobody deployed today.
- Pod logs show the process starts, pulls 1,204 rules from rules-admin (revision 8841), then panics while compiling a specific rule:
    "compiling rule BF-2026-STACKED (tiers=3, stacking=true)"
    "panic: runtime error: index out of range [3] with length 3"
    at internal/rules/tiers.go:88 TierTable.Lookup, called from compileStacked.
- pricing-rules-admin pod is Running and healthy, so it is serving rules normally; the new/edited rule BF-2026-STACKED (a 3-tier stacked rule) is what the engine chokes on. This matches the CrashLoopBackOff cause category "application errors that cause the container to exit" [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#container-restarts-1].

Why it started "a little after 2pm" despite no deploy: the engine fetches rules at startup, and the panic is deterministic on rule BF-2026-STACKED. Any pod restart after that rule was added/edited in rules-admin (revision 8841) will crash. Kubernetes then keeps restarting per the Pod restartPolicy with exponential backoff [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#container-restarts-0].

Fix (owner action, outside the cluster):
1. In rules-admin, revert or correct rule BF-2026-STACKED (the 3-tier stacked rule published in revision 8841) — most likely a tier index is off-by-one so Lookup(3) runs against a 3-element table. Rolling rules-admin back to the revision prior to 8841 will unblock the pods immediately.
2. Once rules-admin serves a valid rule set, the existing pods will exit CrashLoopBackOff on their next restart attempt; no kubectl change is required (the Deployment and images are fine).
3. Follow-up for the pricing-engine team: bounds-check in rules/tiers.go:88 TierTable.Lookup so a bad rule is rejected with a clear error instead of panicking and taking the whole service down.

No cluster-side change is needed or safe to make from here.
